suchomimus:enwiki:4.title: Suchomimus (Suggested synonymy with Baryonyx and Cristatusaurus)

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian), ~

facts.statement: The only known species, S. tenerensis, was described in 1998 by Paul Sereno and colleagues based on fossils found in the Elrhaz Formation.
facts.quote: The only known species is S. tenerensis, originally described in 1998 by paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues from several fossils discovered one year earlier in the Elrhaz Formation.

facts.statement: The specific name 'tenerensis' refers to the Ténéré Desert where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The animal's generic name, which means "crocodile mimic", alludes to its elongated skull and piscivorous adaptations, while the specific name refers to the Ténéré Desert, where the fossils were discovered.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had an elongated, low, and narrow skull that resembled that of crocodilians.
facts.quote: As its generic name suggests, the animal's skull was elongated, low, and narrow, resembling that of crocodilians.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had a relatively short neck and powerfully built forelimbs with a large curved claw on each thumb.
facts.quote: The neck of Suchomimus was relatively short, while its powerfully built forelimbs bore a large, curved claw on each thumb.

facts.statement: A low dorsal sail ran along the midline of its back, constructed from long neural spines.
facts.quote: Along the midline of the animal's back ran a low dorsal sail, built from the long neural spines of its vertebrae.

facts.statement: Suchomimus tenerensis was formally named and described in a study published in Science Magazine on November 13, 1998.
facts.quote: On 13 November 1998, the Science Magazine published a study led by Sereno, formally naming and describing the new genus and species Suchomimus tenerensis based on the fossils discovered during the expedition.

facts.statement: All known fossil specimens are housed in the collections of the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.
facts.quote: All known fossil specimens were recovered from the Elrhaz Formation and are now housed in the paleontological collections of the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.

facts.statement: The holotype, catalogued as MNN GDF500, is a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: The holotype, catalogued as MNN GDF500, consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: Cristatusaurus lapparenti was named by Philippe Taquet and Dale A. Russell more than two months before Suchomimus tenerensis was formally described.
facts.quote: More than two months before S. tenerensis was formally described in the scientific literature, French paleontologist Philippe Taquet and his Canadian colleague Dale A. Russell named another spinosaurid from the Elrhaz Formation, Cristatusaurus lapparenti, based on fragments of jaws and vertebrae.

facts.statement: A 2017 review by Carlos Roberto A. Candeiro and colleagues stated the debate over Suchomimus and Baryonyx is more semantic than scientific, noting they are generally agreed to be distinct related genera.
facts.quote: A 2017 review paper by the Brazilian palaeontologist Carlos Roberto A. Candeiro and colleagues stated that this debate was more in the realm of semantics than science, as it is generally agreed that Suchomimus and Baryonyx are distinct, related genera.

facts.statement: Historical estimates placed Suchomimus at 9.5 to 11 meters in length and 2.5 to 3.8 metric tons in weight.
facts.quote: The size of Suchomimus was historically estimated at 9.5 – 11 m in length, with a weight of 2.5 - 3.8 MT.

facts.statement: In 2007, François Therrien and Donald M. Henderson proposed a 10.3-meter-long Suchomimus weighed over 5.2 metric tons, though they noted this might overestimate spinosaurid sizes.
facts.quote: In 2007, Canadian paleontologists François Therrien and Donald M. Henderson proposed that a 10.3 m long Suchomimus would have weighed more than 5.2 MT based on their ratio between skull length and body length; however, they noted that they might have overestimated the size of spinosaurids (i.e., Suchomimus and Baryonyx).

facts.statement: The skull of Suchomimus is estimated to be about 1.2 meters long.
facts.quote: The skull of Suchomimus is estimated at around 1.2 m in length.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had approximately 122 conical teeth that were slightly curved backward, had fine serrations, and wrinkled enamel.
facts.quote: The jaws had about 122 conical teeth, pointed but not very sharp and curving slightly backwards, with fine serrations and wrinkled enamel.

facts.statement: The tip of Suchomimus's snout featured a 'terminal rosette' of longer teeth, with seven on each side of the upper and lower jaws.
facts.quote: The tip of the snout was enlarged sideways and carried a "terminal rosette" of longer teeth, seven per side in the premaxillae and about the same number in the corresponding part of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Suchomimus had a prominent downward kink behind the snout tip, where the maxilla held the longest teeth in the skull.
facts.quote: The upper jaw had a prominent kink just behind the rosette, protruding downwards; this convexly curved part of the maxilla had the longest teeth of the entire skull.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, Suchomimus had nostrils retracted further back on the skull, positioned behind the premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: The nostrils, unlike in most theropods, were retracted further back on the skull and behind the premaxillary teeth.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had significantly extended, blade-shaped neural spines on its vertebrae that were elongated toward the rear.
facts.quote: Suchomimus had significantly extended neural spines—blade-shaped upward extensions on the vertebrae—which were elongated at the rear back.

facts.statement: The V-shaped furcula of Suchomimus indicates it had a high and narrow trunk.
facts.quote: The furcula was V-shaped and indicates a high and narrow trunk.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had a well-developed ulna with an enormous olecranon, an exceptional trait also shared with Baryonyx.
facts.quote: The ulna of the lower arm was well-developed with an enormous olecranon (upper process set-off from the shaft), an exceptional trait shared with Baryonyx.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had a high ilium and a pubis with a wide front surface and a flattened, rectangular lower end, differing from the boot shape seen in other theropods.
facts.quote: In the pelvis, the ilium (main hip bone) was high. The pubis (pubic bone) had a front surface that was wider than the side surface, and its forward-facing lower end was flattened and rectangular, with a brief flange along the midline, in contrast to the expanded boot shape it had in other theropods.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype Suchomimus was straight, robust, and measured 107 cm in length.
facts.quote: The femur (thighbone) was straight and robust, with a length of 107 cm in the holotype.

facts.statement: In its original description, Suchomimus was placed within Spinosauridae and assigned to the subfamily Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: The authors placed Suchomimus within Spinosauridae and named two subfamilies within this clade, Baryonychinae (all spinosaurids more closely related to Baryonyx) and Spinosaurinae (all spinosaurids closer to Spinosaurus), with Suchomimus assigned to the former.

facts.statement: In 2021, American paleontologist Chris T. Barker and colleagues established the tribe Ceratosuchopsini within Baryonychinae, which includes Ceratosuchops, Riparovenator, and Suchomimus.
facts.quote: Although not ruling out this possibility, American paleontologist Chris T. Barker and his colleagues established in 2021 a new tribe within the Baryonychinae, named Ceratosuchopsini, a clade that includes Ceratosuchops, Riparovenator, and Suchomimus.

facts.statement: Suchomimus was originally described in 1998 by Sereno and colleagues, who identified unique traits including expanded neural spines and a boss on the humerus.
facts.quote: In their original 1998 description of Suchomimus, Sereno and colleagues identified several autapomorphies (unique derived traits) distinguishing it from other theropods: its expanded rear dorsal, sacral, and front caudal neural spines, the robust upper corners of the humerus, and the boss above the humerus' condyle that contacted its hook-shaped radius.

facts.statement: In 2010, British paleontologist Roger Benson considered the superfamily Spinosauroidea a junior synonym of Megalosauroidea.
facts.quote: in 2010, the British palaeontologist Roger Benson considered this a junior synonym of Megalosauroidea (an older name).

facts.statement: Suchomimus is classified within the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Suchomimus belongs to the subfamily Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Baryonychinae

facts.statement: Suchomimus was named and described by paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues in 1998.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado y descrito por el paleontólogo Paul Sereno y colegas en 1998

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 112 million years ago, in the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 a 112 millones de años, en el Aptiense

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es África

facts.statement: Suchomimus has an elongated and shallow skull similar to that of a crocodile, which inspired its generic name.
facts.quote: El cráneo alargado y poco profundo de Suchomimus, similar al de un cocodrilo, le otorga su nombre genérico

facts.statement: The specific name S. tenerensis refers to the Teneré Desert, the locality where the first remains were found.
facts.quote: el nombre específico S. tenerensis alude a la localidad donde fueron encontrados sus primeros restos, el desierto de Teneré

facts.statement: Isotopic geochemical evidence supports a semi-aquatic foraging habit for Suchomimus.
facts.quote: Isotopic geochemical lines of evidence also support a semi-aquatic foraging habit for Suchomimus

facts.statement: Milner suggested in 2003 that spinosaurids originated in Laurasia during the Jurassic and dispersed into Gondwana via the Iberian land bridge.
facts.quote: Milner suggested in 2003 that spinosaurids originated in Laurasia during the Jurassic and dispersed via the Iberian land bridge into Gondwana

facts.statement: The direction of dispersal between Europe and Africa for spinosaurids is still unknown.
facts.quote: The direction of the dispersal between Europe and Africa is still unknown

facts.statement: The initial estimate for the length of the Suchomimus type specimen was between 10.3 and 11 meters, with a weight estimated between 2.7 and 5.2 tonnes.
facts.quote: La longitud del espécimen tipo de Suchomimus, un subadulto, se estimó inicialmente entre 10,3 a 11 metros, con un peso estimado de entre 2,7 y 5,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul provided lower estimates of 9.5 meters in length and 2.5 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul, sin embargo, dio estimaciones más bajas de 9,5 metros y 2,5 toneladas en 2010.

facts.statement: A 2020 study adjusted the body mass of the holotype to 3.26 tonnes based on femoral circumference.
facts.quote: un estudio de 2020 moderó la masa corporal del holotipo en 3,26 toneladas en función de la circunferencia femoral.

facts.statement: Unlike other giant theropods, Suchomimus had a very long and low snout and narrow jaws formed by the forward expansion of premaxillae, frontal bones, and the posterior ramus of the maxillae.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros terópodos gigantes tenía un hocico muy largo y bajo, y quijadas estrechas formadas por una expansión hacia adelante de los premaxilares, huesos frontales del hocico y la rama trasera de los maxilares, hueso principal de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: The jaws were studded with about 120 teeth that were not very sharp, slightly curved backward, and had fine striations and rough enamel.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas estaban tachonadas con unos 120 dientes no muy agudos y curvados levemente hacia atrás, con finas estrías y esmalte rugoso.

facts.statement: The snout tip was bulbous and carried a rosette of longer teeth than the rest, with seven on each side of the premaxillae and approximately the same number on the corresponding part of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: La extremidad del hocico era abultada y llevaba un rosetón de dientes más largos que el resto, siete por lado en los premaxilares y aproximadamente el mismo número en la parte correspondiente de la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Further back, there were at least 22 teeth on each side of the upper jaw in the maxilla, while the entire side of the lower jaw had 32 teeth in the dentary bone.
facts.quote: Más atrás, había al menos 22 dientes por lado de la mandíbula superior en el maxilar superior, mientras que todo el lado de la mandíbula inferior llevaba 32 dientes en el hueso dentario.

facts.statement: The nasal openings, unlike in most theropods, were retracted further back in the skull and behind the premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales, a diferencia de la mayoría de los terópodos, estaban retraídas más atrás en el cráneo y detrás de los dientes premaxilares.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had approximately 16 dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Había alrededor de 16 vértebras dorsales.

facts.statement: The arm musculature drove considerable-sized hand claws, with the first digit being the largest at 19 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: La musculatura del brazo impulsaba garras de mano de tamaño considerables, siendo la del primer dedo la más grande con una longitud de 19 centímetros.

facts.statement: The femur was straight and robust, measuring 107 centimeters in length in the holotype.
facts.quote: El fémur, el hueso del muslo, era recto y robusto, con una longitud de 107 centímetros en el holotipo.

facts.statement: Researchers generally view Suchomimus as a large creature that usually fed on fish and walked through the Sahara over 100 million years ago when it was a swampy paradise.
facts.quote: La impresión general que plantean los investigadores es la de una criatura de gran porte, que se alimentaba usualmente de peces, y que hace más de 100 millones de años deambulaba por el Sáhara cuando este era un vergel pantanoso.

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Suchomimus belongs to the parent group Ceratosuchopsini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratosuchopsini

facts.statement: Suchomimus is classified in the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Suchomimus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
